assertions.description: Output mentions Stripe Checkout reconciliation via client_reference_id
Output distinguishes Checkout metadata from subscription_data.metadata
Output covers webhook deduplication or duplicate-event handling
Output explains user-billed versus tenant-billed separation
Output mentions Stripe Entitlements or entitlement projection
Output mentions stripeAccountId for multi-account or multi-entity setups
Output does not claim every SaaS must use one Stripe customer per user
assertions.check: not_contains: "always create one Stripe customer per user"

assertions.description: Output stays focused enough for operator use
Output mentions shared resolver updates for new price IDs or billing intervals
Output says new recurring prices should be created instead of mutating an existing amount in place
assertions.check: contains_one_of: ["create a new Price", "new Price", "archive the old price", "legacy price", "lookup_key"]

test_cases.input: We use Stripe Checkout in NeonDash. How should I map client_reference_id, metadata, and subscription_data.metadata so the webhook can reconcile the right user or tenant?
Should our SaaS create one Stripe customer per user or one per clinic workspace? Explain user-billed vs tenant-billed and how that affects Drizzle data modeling.
We may bill different legal entities in separate Stripe accounts. What should NeonDash persist to avoid mixing subscriptions and entitlements across accounts?
I need to add an annual Stripe price to NeonDash and keep webhook interval detection working. What shared resolver and catalog rules do I need to update?
The Pro monthly amount changed. Should I edit the existing Stripe recurring price or create a new one, and how should NeonDash treat the old price for existing subscribers?
